newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slip in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slip in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks began on a weak note on Monday morning, with caution about interest rates prompting investors to continue taking profits after a slide in share prices last week, brokers said.

"It's the same old story that we have been looking at -- interest rates in the States," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. "The Dow Jones doing intra-day corrections is scaring some people," he added.
The Hang Seng Index was down 97.78 points at 13,281.77.
Turnover was HK$2.43 billion after the first hour of trade.
Analysts said a continued rise in the U.S. long bond yield had made investors nervous, particularly with fresh economic data due out of the United States this week.

The U.S. long bond fell 12/32 on Friday to yield 6.89 percent. The Dow industrials slipped 59.27 points to 6,696.48 after falling to an intra-day low of 6,662.23. The Hang Seng index fell 3.44 percent last week.
"Again we are subject to profit-taking," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
He expected the blue-chip index to test 13,000 points this week but said prices should find support there.
"Red chips are generally doing better than most," said Mak.
Shares in CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.10 to HK$38.50, Shanghai Industrial gained HK$0.35 to HK$27.45 and China Resources added HK$0.20 to HK$16.00.
However, concern about Giordano's expansion plans in China pushed the stock HK$1.15 lower to HK$3.90.

The stock resumed trading on Monday after the company said negotiations relating to the setting up of new Giordano retail outlets in Beijing and Shanghai had not been concluded and it was continuing to address regulatory procedural demands concerning its operations in China.
Conglomerates and banks led Monday's decline.
In the banking sector, HSBC Holdings was off HK$2.50 at HK$175.00 and Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.50 at HK$90.75.
Among the conglomerates, Hutchison shed HK$1.00 to HK$60.25 and Wharf Holdings was down HK$0.50 at HK$36.10. Swire Pacific fell HK$0.50 to HK$73.25.

China Light rose HK$1.10 to HK$34.20. The company posted a first interim dividend on Friday of HK$0.34 compared with HK$0.32. It also said its proposed power plant project in China's Shandong province had been approved by China's State Council.
